landmarks.name: Chocolate Hills
landmarks.writeup: A unique geological formation of over 1,200 symmetrical hills that turn brown in the dry season, located in Bohol.

wiki.extract: The Chocolate Hills are a geological formation in the Philippine province of Bohol. A minimum of 1,260 hills, and possibly over 1,776, spread over an area of more than 50 square kilometers (20 sq mi). They are covered in green grass that turns a chocolate-brown during the dry season, hence the name.

landmarks.name: Rizal Park
landmarks.writeup: A historical urban park in Manila dedicated to national hero José Rizal.

wiki.extract: Rizal Park, Luneta, also known as Rizal Park, Luneta Park, or simply Luneta, is a historic urban park located in Ermita, Manila, Philippines. It is one of the largest urban parks in the country, covering an area of 58 hectares. The area now occupied by the park was known as Bagumbayan during the Spanish colonial period. It is adjacent to the historic walled city of Intramuros.

landmarks.name: Taal Volcano
landmarks.writeup: One of the world's smallest active volcanoes, located on an island in Taal Lake.

wiki.extract: Taal Volcano, also known as Taal Caldera, is a large caldera filled by Taal Lake in the Philippines. Located in the province of Batangas about 50 kilometers (31 mi) south of Manila, the volcano is the second most active volcano in the country, with 39 recorded historical eruptions, all concentrated on Volcano Island, near the middle of Taal Lake. The caldera was formed by prehistoric eruptions between less than 670,000 and less than 6,000 years ago. The cones Batulao, Macolod, and Sungay are remnants of the early pre-caldera Taal system, with Batulao being the earliest known cone.

landmarks.name: Banaue Rice Terraces
landmarks.writeup: Ancient terraces carved into the mountains of Ifugao, often called the 'Eighth Wonder of the World.'

wiki.extract: The Banaue Rice Terraces are terraces that were carved into the mountains of Banaue, Ifugao, in the Philippines, by the ancestors of the Igorot people. The terraces were built with minimal equipment, largely by hand. The terraces are located approximately 1,500 meters above sea level. These are fed by an ancient irrigation system from the rainforests above the terraces.

landmarks.name: Intramuros
landmarks.writeup: A historic walled city in Manila dating back to Spanish colonial times.

wiki.extract: Intramuros is the 0.67-square-kilometer (0.26 sq mi) historic walled area within the city of Manila, the capital of the Philippines. It is administered by the Intramuros Administration with the help of the city government of Manila.

cultural_events.name: Sinulog Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual cultural and religious festival in Cebu honoring the Santo Niño with street dancing and parades.

wiki.extract: The Sinulog Festival is an annual Filipino cultural and religious festival held on the third Sunday of January in Cebu, with the center of the activities being in Cebu City; and is the core of Santo Niño Christian celebrations in the country.

cultural_events.name: Ati-Atihan Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A week-long festival in Kalibo featuring tribal dances and music to honor the Santo Niño.

wiki.extract: The Kalibo Santo Niño–Ati-Atihan Festival, also simply called Ati-Atihan Festival, is a Philippine festival held annually in January in honor of the Santo Niño in several towns of the province of Aklan, Panay Island. The biggest celebration is held during the third Sunday of January in the town of Kalibo, the province's capital. The name Ati-Atihan means "to imitate the Ati people".

cultural_events.name: Pahiyas Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A colorful harvest festival in Lucban where houses are decorated with agricultural produce.

wiki.extract: Lucban, officially the Municipality of Lucban, is a municipality in the province of Quezon, Philippines. According to the 2024 census, it has a population of 54,134 people.

food_writeup: Filipino cuisine is characterized by bold flavors and a mix of indigenous, Spanish, Chinese, and American influences, featuring dishes like adobo, sinigang, lechon, and pancit.
brief_history: The Philippines was colonized by Spain for over 300 years, followed by American rule after the Spanish-American War. It gained independence in 1946 and has since developed as a democratic republic with a diverse cultural heritage.
current_conflicts: Ongoing territorial disputes in the South China Sea and internal conflicts with insurgent groups such as the New People's Army and Islamist militants.
